claim: The command guard change K4 (scripts/hooks/secret_path_guard.py, sha256 d4d4bef271df8973cca7f6e7fa6f70be717bec7a909f35e3b0eeea4ce67d65a4, 275,593 bytes) adds runner-command reading, bounded interpreter reading and OmniRoute management-route, manager-environment, store, ps and canary rules on top of the K3 guard (sha256 a70a056fc27524c65ea5ce4db43fe712cabb44cf9b171866abf805d7306d3b51, PR #511). On 2026-10-01 the coordinator replayed 1,490 documented repository commands through K4 against K3 and against the installed guard (sha256 f9be81b240762dc58da874f135040d182ca9fb5e9056ab9b8a977dd909453244): 0 newly blocked, 0 loosened and 0 reason changed against each. The acceptance oracle found 0 adjusted and 0 reason mismatches over 338 cases, and a scan of 16,174 distinct lines and blocks from 9,245 tracked files found 0 newly blocked and 0 loosened against K3. The repair worker's mutation gate killed 461 of 461 mutants by failures of named permanent tests. A read-only GPT-6 re-check of the one repair round found every finding of the GPT-6 verification and the Opus review fixed, apart from stale metadata in an untracked handoff, and no input that K3 refuses and K4 allows outside the contract's form F across 8,602 differential inputs. Through a real hook process the verification's two timeout generators answered in 0.20 and 0.22 s. The re-check found five further items, recorded as residuals.
limitations: Local integration on one host plus read-only cross-family reviews, not a proof: the checks compare text heuristics on finite corpora (the repository's tables, fenced commands, tracked files, generated mutations and the reviewers' differential inputs), and a review that finds nothing does not show that nothing exists.

Evidence classes differ: the replay, the oracle, the corpus scan, the gitleaks ancestry scan and the targeted suites were run by the coordinator on the final head; the mutation gate and the differential counts come from the repair worker's and the re-check's recorded output, not from a coordinator rerun.

The targeted suites' one failure is by design: test_host_profile_copy_is_verbatim compares the installed host copy with the repository file, and the host copy stays the installed guard until K3 and K4 are merged and reinstalled after the Gate A window closes.

test_k4_timing compares one CPU-time sample per size: in a whole-suite run under host load its k4_shell_words ratio check failed once (0.091 s against the 0.08 s bound that the 0.01 s floor sets), and three isolated runs passed. A noisy runner can fail it the same way.

Residuals carried to the next guard change: two gateway forms that K3 and K4 both allow, a Request passed to urlopen by keyword after its body (urlopen(data=b"x", url=r)) and an augmented member assignment (r.full_url += "/x"); two false refusals K4 introduced, an incomplete computed argv item (subprocess.run(["printenv" + "-safe"]) refuses environment_dump) and a command -v lookup read as an assignment before a keyring store (keyring_store_literal); and a generated 193,560-character urllib command whose urlopen calls reuse one Request, which the re-check measured at about 1.9 s through the real hook, below the 10 s hook timeout and above the 1 s target.

Commit identity: the re-check reviewed commit 58dde8ef. Its history was then rewritten so a helper-name tuple no longer reads as a gitleaks generic-api-key match (one test line reordered in four commits) and rebased with K3 onto main; the guard bytes are unchanged (the sha256 above).
evidence_class: local integration (documented-command replay, acceptance oracle, tracked-file scan, gitleaks ancestry scan and the targeted unit suites on this host, run by the coordinator), the repair worker's recorded mutation gate, and read-only cross-family reviews: a GPT-6 (gpt-6-astra, effort max) verification and re-check and an Opus review
